coordinates.note: Campus-grade: the OpenStreetMap outline of the plant. The TAO detector is in a basement 9.6 m underground, 44 m from a reactor core (the 2020 design report said about 30 m); its position inside the plant is not published in the sources read.

depth.note: Depth of the detector location below ground level.

summary.plain: A basement room at the Taishan nuclear power plant in Guangdong, China, nine and a half metres underground and several tens of metres from a reactor core, where the JUNO-TAO detector is being installed.
summary.technical: Basement at -9.6 m (a few metres of water-equivalent overburden) at 44 m from a 4.6 GW_th Taishan core (design report: about 30 m). Marked with a campus-grade point for the plant.
